independent_computations_performed.purpose: Independent check of the contract's own pre-registered comparison_test_power_check claim ('powered to detect ~2x or more, NOT a sub-20% relative difference') against the actual matched-pair cell's parameters.
independent_computations_performed.method: Two-proportion normal-approximation power formula (pooled variance under H0, unpooled under H1) at n=20000, p1=613/20000, for relative differences 5%-200%; cross-checked with a 300-replication Monte Carlo simulation using the RECOMP-5 hypergeometric Fisher-exact implementation (not scipy).
key_outputs: 20% relative difference: 92.5% power (normal approx) / 94.7% (Monte Carlo, 300 reps) -- the design IS well-powered at 20%, contradicting the contract's own claim.
80% power is reached already at a ~16.4% relative difference, not '2x' (100%).
At the actually-observed ~10.8% relative difference: ~46.5% power (normal approx) / 42.3% (Monte Carlo) -- moderate, not negligible.
Conclusion: the contract's pre-registered power characterization is materially wrong for the specific (N=580,tau=4) cell Stage 0 actually found; it was written generically before that cell was known.
